title: PVLedger database specification — draft, portable schema contract
status: Draft: structural baseline verified against SQLite; user-defined design choices recorded; business descriptions remain editable
scope: Target database design and original-source provenance, tables, keys, relationships, user-approved datatype/storage decisions, dialect portability, and unresolved business semantics; no data included
database_description: Proposed: personal-finance application storage for users, banking accounts, expenses, debts, taxes, reference data, and settings.

assumptions_and_open_questions: Confirm/replace inferred functional descriptions and define interest, balances, amounts and billing-date business semantics.
Unix timestamps use integer seconds since the UTC epoch as the draft convention; confirm unit seconds versus milliseconds. All target date and billing_date columns are INTEGER.
Application-defined integer states (examples 1,2,3) have no enum map or SQL CHECK constraints yet; define their meanings in the application.
pvl_access_rights is a placeholder; future authorization table relationships remain undecided.
The target table pvl_expenses_planned corrects the original pvl_expenses_planed; decide how to migrate any existing database, views, and application queries.
Password storage is user-specified as MD5 hashes. MD5 is unsuitable for secure password storage; prefer Argon2id/scrypt/bcrypt for new deployments and plan a migration.
Decide whether to migrate financial REAL fields to fixed-precision DECIMAL/NUMERIC(p,s).
Define username size, case sensitivity and NULL behavior; source unique rule permits NULL.
Decide whether pvl_settings should be a singleton; source allows multiple rows.
Define country ISO standard, currency identifiers and any uniqueness constraints.
Define recurrence rules for pvl_expenses_recurring (frequency/next-run logic not in database).
Define FK on-update/on-delete behavior if default NO ACTION is not desired.
Decide indexes for referencing FK columns and common access patterns.

sqlite.NUMERIC: Only found in original SQL for pvl_expenses.date; target is INTEGER
sqlite.identity: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY; AUTOINCREMENT where present in source
sqlite.application_integer_codes: INTEGER with values assigned and interpreted by application; no CHECK constraint
sqlite.md5_password_digest: TEXT (convention: 32 hexadecimal characters; no CHECK constraint)

postgresql.INTEGER: BIGINT to preserve the possible 64-bit integer range of SQLite
postgresql.NUMERIC: Not needed for the target timestamp columns
postgresql.identity: BIGINT GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY except settings unless separately decided
postgresql.unix_timestamps: BIGINT, epoch seconds in UTC (do not implicitly convert to TIMESTAMP)
postgresql.application_integer_codes: INTEGER or BIGINT (consistent with selected range), not BOOLEAN
postgresql.md5_password_digest: TEXT or VARCHAR(32); MD5 is insecure for password storage

mysql_mariadb.INTEGER: BIGINT to preserve the possible 64-bit integer range of SQLite
mysql_mariadb.TEXT: TEXT; use suitable VARCHAR(n) for uniquely indexed username
mysql_mariadb.NUMERIC: Not needed for the target timestamp columns
mysql_mariadb.identity: BIGINT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY except settings unless separately decided
mysql_mariadb.unix_timestamps: BIGINT, epoch seconds in UTC (avoid implicit TIMESTAMP range/timezone conversions)
mysql_mariadb.application_integer_codes: INT or BIGINT, not BOOLEAN/TINYINT(1) shorthand
mysql_mariadb.md5_password_digest: VARCHAR(32) or TEXT; MD5 is insecure for password storage

changes: All date and billing_date fields use 64-bit-compatible INTEGER Unix timestamps in the target schema (seconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z used as the draft unit).
Application-defined integer codes, e.g. 1, 2, 3, are retained for status and state/flag fields; no DB-level enum or boolean coercion.
Access control remains a placeholder, without inferred relationships.
Corrected pvl_expenses_planed to pvl_expenses_planned in the target schema; source name retained for provenance and migrations.
pvl_users.password will contain an MD5 hash in hexadecimal form; security warning documented.

date_storage.unit_status: draft convention; confirm seconds rather than milliseconds if application differs
date_storage.notes: Unix timestamps represent instants in UTC. If billing_date is actually intended as a day of month rather than an instant, its business semantics will need separate review.

state_code_storage.notes: The source names may suggest booleans, but they are integer codes, not restricted to TRUE/FALSE or 0/1. Examples are not an exhaustive allowed-value list.

access_control.future_work: Model authorization, roles and user associations later; do not add FKs now.

naming.other_identifier_names: Retained as defined by source; id_countries is awkward grammar but not a spelling error, so no silent rename.

password_storage.security_warning: MD5 is unsuitable for password storage: it is fast and vulnerable to offline guessing. New systems should prefer Argon2id, scrypt or bcrypt; document a future migration path.
